 Injury Notes: Missi, Murphy, Barnes, Leonard, Christie, Penda, More
 By Rory Maher |
 at November 14, 2026 1:39 pm 
 The Pelicans are expected to get Yves Missi back for Saturday’s game vs. Denver, tweets Will Guillory of The Athletic. The third-year center is officially listed as probable to play in tonight’s contest after being sidelined for the past 11 contests due to a left knee contusion/bone bruise.
 A 6’11” big man who played one season of college basketball at Baylor, Missi was New Orleans’ opening night starting center. The 22-year-old performed well in that three-point loss to Indiana, finishing with 13 points, 14 rebounds, five assists, three blocks and two steals in 30 minutes, before getting injured in the second quarter of the team’s second game of the season.
 It’s unclear if Missi will assume the starting role again immediately after returning. It wouldn’t be surprising if he comes off the bench for a while first following a three-week absence. Missi will be eligible for a rookie scale extension next offseason.
 While Missi is expected to be back, starting wing Trey Murphy III continues to be hampered by bilateral patellar tendinopathy. The 6’8″ forward will miss his fourth straight game Saturday due to the knee issues.
 We have more injury-related updates from around the NBA:
 Star forward Scottie Barnes (left adductor strain) has missed the Raptors ’ last four games and is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday vs. New York, per Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca ( Twitter link ). Barnes went through part of Saturday’s practice. Kawhi Leonard , meanwhile, continues to do individual on-court work, Grange adds. Leonard, who was named Finals MVP when Toronto captured the title in 2019, has been limited to two appearances this season because of left knee swelling. The seven-time All-NBA forward is expected to be reevaluated early next week.
 Mavericks guard Max Christie has been downgraded to doubtful for Saturday’s game against Cleveland because of a left ankle sprain, according to Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News ( Twitter link ). Christie was a bright spot for the Mavericks last season and started the first seven games of 2026/27 before suffering a hip injury that caused him to miss one game. Since he returned to action, the former second-round pick has only averaged 9.5 minutes per game over four appearances amid a shooting slump. However, head coach Dusty May recently backed Christie, writes Grant Afseth of Dallas Sports Journal . “ We haven’t lost any faith in Max ,” May said of Christie, who holds an $8.9MM player option for next season. “ I think he’s had a little bit of bad luck this year where he’s defending at a high level and guys have made hard shots. [He] just [needs to] continue to play with confidence to get back to where he’s not over-thinking, and just let the game come to him and play. He brings a lot of things to this team that we need. We just have a whole lot of really good players and some other guys are playing a little bit better at this moment .”
 Second-year forward Noah Penda is making progress in his recovery from a partially torn right hamstring, an injury he suffered in the Magic ’s preseason finale on Oct. 16, as Jason Beede of The Orlando Sentinel writes. There’s no timeline for Penda’s return, but the Frenchman told Beede he’s “feeling better” and is glad he was able to resume light on-court work so quickly after he sustained the injury. “ I didn’t know what coming back from a big injury would look like ,” Penda said. “ I’m a guy that needs to move a lot and I love basketball before everything. So, I was kind of relieved when you saw me in New York shooting (three weeks ago). It’s good mentally to be able to do all of this stuff this quickly. I don’t know how much time I have left but I know that at least I’m able to touch the ball and get on the court, and it feels good .”
 Injuries (the Thunder, Anthony Edwards , Tyrese Haliburton , Jalen Duren , Leonard, etc.) have been a major storyline in the first few weeks of the season and there are no indications that will change anytime soon, according to John Hollinger of The Athletic . Last season, only 36 players missed fewer than five games; during the 2015/16 campaign, that number was at 97. Injuries are the primary reason rosters were expanded from 12/13 to 15 and then 15 to 18 once two-way contracts were implemented, Hollinger observes, and teams have been forced to utilize all of their players more often. While health has always played an important role in postseason success, it seems more critical than ever to have good injury luck at the right time, rather than having the best team on paper, Hollinger writes.
